studies.Reference: The predictive role of the total potassium intake and odds of breast cancer: a case-control study.
studies.Authors: Ahmadirad H, Norouzzadeh M, Teymoori F, Jahromi MK, Farhadnejad H, Babrpanjeh M, Mokhtari E, Heidari Z, Mirmiran P, Rashidkhani B
studies.exposure_measurement_supporting_text: A validated semi-quantitative 168-item food frequency questionnaire was used to compute the potassium intake.

extraction_supporting_text.sample_size: The study included 134 newly diagnosed cases of BC and 267 controls.
extraction_supporting_text.effect_size: higher total potassium intake was associated with decreased odds of BC (OR: 0.35, 95%CI: 0.19-0.62, P for trend < 0.001)
extraction_supporting_text.effect_direction: higher total potassium intake was associated with decreased odds of BC
extraction_supporting_text.outcome_definition: risk of breast cancer (BC) among Iranian adult women

studies.Reference: Association between empirically derived nutrient patterns and breast cancer: a case-control study in a Middle Eastern country.
studies.Authors: Dehghani F, Sasanfar B, Toorang F, Zendehdel K, Salehi-Abargouei A
studies.comparison_type: Highest vs Lowest adherence to nutrient pattern 3 (rich in potassium, fiber, vitamin C)

extraction_supporting_text.effect_direction: A significant inverse relationship was observed between adherence to nutrient pattern 3 and the risk of BC

headline.funnel_interpretation: Insufficient studies to perform formal publication bias testing.
headline.results_interpretation: The pooled analysis of 2 studies yielded an effect size of 0.55 (95% CI: 0.3–1.03), indicating no statistically significant association between potassium and breast cancer. Although the point estimate suggests a potential inverse relationship, the confidence interval includes the null. These findings were accompanied by substantial heterogeneity (I² = 74.66%), reflecting considerable variability across studies.
